target_customer: Food companies and meat producers that want to make cultivated beef and need a cheaper, scalable bioprocess
problem: Cultivated meat is too expensive and hard to scale, mainly because of growth media cost and bioreactor scale-up.
business_model: Technology and platform partnerships with food companies, asset-light production licensing

founders.name: Patricia Bubner
founders.background_notes: YC page states she has raised over $15M.

founders.name: Samet Yildirim
founders.background_notes: Company describes both founders as having biopharma mammalian cell scale-up experience.

competitors.name: Upside Foods (formerly Memphis Meats)
competitors.funding_then: Hundreds of millions raised in total, sources differ

technical_complexity.rationale: Scaling mammalian cell culture for food at a cost near commodity beef was an unsolved research and engineering problem, needing bioprocess know-how, media cost reduction and hardware.

defensibility.rationale: Claimed proprietary bioware and computational process models, but the field had many well funded rivals and the cost claim was not independently proven.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large meat companies invested in or partnered with cultivated startups rather than copying. Orbillion itself was absorbed by a peer, Fork & Good, in 2025.

market_need_then: Cultivated meat funding peaked at about $989M in 2021 per AgFunder, driven by climate and animal welfare interest and the need for lower cost production.

branding.domain_note: Used orbillion.com, no acquisition story found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical and cost focused, claims price parity

branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage focused on a public tasting and Demo Day, not on the brand itself.

brand_strength.rationale: Trade press covered the company, but no sources show mascot, community or brand driven growth.

outcome_analysis: Orbillion raised a seed in 2021 at the peak of cultivated meat funding and an additional round in 2024 that brought its total to about $15M, as the sector's funding fell sharply in 2023. Without a reported price or breakout commercial product, it was acquired by pork peer Fork & Good in October 2025 as part of sector consolidation, combining IP and production sites. The exit looks like a consolidation outcome rather than a clear win, and terms are not public.
